about.title: Modeling with Linear Functions
about.length_note: About 35 minutes, a little over the usual half hour. There are three separate ideas: building an equation, saying what its numbers mean, and reading a graph as a story. Each gets its own worked example and a check question. You can pause after beat 12 and come back for the graph half.

4.5 Use the Slope-Intercept Form of an Equation of a Line - Elementary Algebra 2e

say.text: Welcome. Today we turn real stories into equations, say what the numbers mean, and read graphs like stories.
First, one word: a model. It is an equation, function or shape we use to stand in for a real-life situation.
Our models are lines, written y = mx + b. Two numbers do the work. The first is m, the rate of change: how much y changes for each 1 more of x.
The second is b, the initial value. It is where the story starts, the value of y when x is 0.
Here is a story. Andy has 5 dollars and saves 2 dollars every week. The start is 5 and the change is 2 per week, so y = 2x + 5.

ask.q: Sam has 10 dollars and saves 3 dollars each week. What is the rate of change?
ask.why: The rate of change is the 'per' number, how much changes each week. The 10 dollars is the starting amount, not the rate.

say.text: The pattern: the 'per' number multiplies x, and the starting number is added on its own. A bike rental with a 6 dollar fee plus 4 dollars per hour is y = 4x + 6.

show.text: per hour (rate): 4, goes with x || fee at the start: 6, added once

ask.q: A skate rental costs a 3 dollar fee plus 2 dollars per hour. Which equation fits?
ask.why: The 2 dollars per hour grows with the hours, so it multiplies x. The 3 dollar fee is paid once, even at 0 hours, so it is added. That makes y = 2x + 3.

say.text: Some things go down. A tank holds 51 liters and loses 5 liters each minute. The rate is negative: y = -5x + 51.

show.text: going down means m is negative

ask.q: In y = -3x + 20, what does the -3 tell you?
ask.right: y goes down by 3 for each 1 more of x
wrong: y goes up by 3 for each 1 more of x
y goes down by 20 for each 1 more of x
ask.why: The number multiplying x is the rate of change. A negative rate means y falls as x grows. The 20 is the starting value.

say.text: So far the story handed us the numbers. Sometimes we only get two data points. Then we work out m and b ourselves.
Step one is the slope: change in y divided by change in x. For (2, 18) and (5, 33), that is 33 minus 18 over 5 minus 2. 15 over 3 is 5.

ask.q: Two points are (1, 7) and (3, 13). What is the slope?
ask.why: Change in y is 13 - 7 = 6. Change in x is 3 - 1 = 2. Then 6 divided by 2 is 3. Stopping at 6 forgets to divide. The 2 is only the x change. 1/3 turns the fraction upside down.

say.text: Step two is b. Put the slope and one point into y = mx + b. With the point (2, 18): 18 = 5 times 2 plus b. That is 18 = 10 + b, so b = 8.

ask.q: For (1, 7) and (3, 13) the slope is 3. Use the point (1, 7). What is b?
ask.why: Put the numbers in: 7 = 3(1) + b. That is 7 = 3 + b, so b = 4. The 7 is the y of the point, not b. Adding the slope to 7 does not solve the equation.

say.text: Step three is a check. Try the other point: 5 times 5 plus 8 is 33. It matches, so our model is y = 5x + 8.
Now the meaning, with units. Say the points were weeks and dollars saved. The 5 is 5 dollars more each week. The 8 is 8 dollars at week 0.

show.text: 5: dollars saved per week (rate of change) || 8: dollars at week 0 (initial value)

ask.q: A tank model is y = -5x + 51, with liters and minutes. What does the 51 mean?
ask.right: The tank holds 51 liters at minute 0
wrong: The tank loses 51 liters every minute
The tank is empty after 51 minutes
ask.why: b is the value of y when x is 0. That is 51 liters at the start. The loss each minute is the rate, which is 5 liters per minute.

say.text: On a graph, b is where the line crosses the vertical axis. The slope sets the tilt: up if positive, down if negative.

show.text: A straight line starts at 8 on the vertical axis and climbs 5 for every 1 step to the right.

ask.q: A line crosses the vertical axis at 4 and slopes down as you move right. Which equation is it?
ask.why: It crosses at 4, so b = 4. It goes down, so m is negative. Only y = -2x + 4 has both.

say.text: Now graphs as stories. Read a graph from left to right, like reading a story. Time runs along the bottom, and the line shows what changes.
A story has three kinds of parts. Going up is increasing, where the rate is positive. Going down is decreasing, where the rate is negative. Flat is constant.

show.text: Up = increasing || Down = decreasing || Flat (horizontal) = constant

say.text: Try one. Jo walks away from home to a shop at a steady pace, stays in the shop, then walks home faster. The graph shows distance from home against minutes.

show.text: A line rises steadily, goes flat for a while, then falls steeply down to zero.

ask.q: While Jo is in the shop, what does the line do?
ask.why: Time keeps passing, but Jo's distance from home does not change. So the line runs flat, and a flat line is constant.

say.text: Now the other direction: sketching a graph from words. Name each axis with its unit. Mark the start. Then draw one part at a time.

show.text: 1. Label both axes, with units || 2. Mark the starting point || 3. Draw each part in turn

say.text: Here is a tub. It starts with 10 cm of water and fills steadily for 6 minutes to 40 cm. It stays there 4 minutes. Then it drains steadily to 0 in 5 minutes.

show.text: Height in cm against minutes. A line climbs from 10 to 40, runs flat, then falls steeply to 0.

ask.q: Which part of the tub graph is steepest?
wrong: The part where the height stays the same
ask.why: The rates are +5 cm per minute filling, 0 while it stays, and -8 cm per minute draining. Steepness is the size of the rate. 8 is the biggest, and the minus sign only means the line tilts down.

say.text: One last care. Real data is rarely perfectly straight, so a line may only fit for some values.

ask.q: A candle model is y = -2x + 20, with height in cm and x in hours. Does it make sense at 15 hours?
ask.right: No. It gives -10 cm, which is impossible, so the model only works up to 10 hours
wrong: Yes, a model works for every x
Yes, the candle is 10 cm below the table
ask.why: Plug in 15: -2(15) + 20 = -10. A candle cannot have a negative height. The candle is gone at 10 hours, so the model only fits from 0 to 10.

say.text: Let's put it all together. A taxi ride of 3 miles costs 9 dollars. A ride of 7 miles costs 17 dollars.

show.text: Points: (3, 9) and (7, 17) || Find m, then b, then check

ask.why: Slope: (17 - 9) / (7 - 3) = 8/4 = 2. Then 9 = 2(3) + b gives b = 3. Check the other point: 2(7) + 3 = 17. The choice y = 4x - 3 fits the first ride but gives 25 for 7 miles.

say.text: Same taxi, now the meaning. Say it with units.

ask.q: In y = 2x + 3, what does the 3 mean?
ask.right: The ride costs 3 dollars before any miles are driven, a starting fee
wrong: The ride costs 3 dollars per mile
The taxi goes 3 miles per minute
ask.why: The 3 is b, the value when x is 0 miles. It is a fee paid at the start. The 2 is the 'per' number, 2 dollars per mile.

say.text: To wrap up: find m from two points, find b by substituting, check, and say what both mean with units. Next class we compare two functions.

show.text: m = change in y / change in x || b = y when x is 0 || Up, down, flat = increasing, decreasing, constant || Check the model makes sense

other_side.claim: A straight line is a good model for real situations.
other_side.other_view: Often it is, but curriculum authors point out that real data is rarely perfectly linear. A line may fit only some values, or different lines may fit different time periods. Part of modeling is judging whether a line is reasonable and for which values.
